title: SCOPE: Evolving Symbolic World for Planning in Open-Ended Environments
claim: Existing methods rely on incomplete, static, non-adaptive symbolic representations; our framework adds active exploration and memory to evolve a complete, adaptive one.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right: red disadvantages, central framework, blue advantages; color-coded
description: Three side-by-side dashed-border panels. The left red panel, titled 'Existing Disadvantages', shows an incomplete, static symbolic world. A house icon (the real environment) sits next to a 'not equal' sign and a symbolic-world window with red X marks, labeled 'Gap'. Below it, tasks A and B each feed feedback to a robot, with no knowledge shared ('Isolated'). The center black-bordered 'Framework' panel is a pipeline. Env and image go into a GPT-style module that constructs or evolves the symbolic world. Feedback then refines the action plan and evolves the symbolic world, with a SASMem database. Black arrows mark the existing pipeline and blue arrows mark the SCOPE additions. The right blue panel, titled 'SCOPE Advantages', shows the environment approximately equal to a complete symbolic world ('Bridge'). Cross-env and cross-task feedback flows into an adaptive SASMem database. The eye goes first to the colored headers.
caption: Comparison of existing method and SCOPE. In the middle illustration, black arrows denote the pipeline used by existing methods; \textbf{blue arrows} highlight SCOPE extensions.
abstract: Recent works have explored integrating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with classical planners that rely on symbolic representations of planning problems to generate long-horizon plans for complex embodied tasks. However, in open-ended environments, these symbolic representations obtained from perception are often incomplete, leading to suboptimal performance. To address this, we introduce SCOPE, a self-adaptive symbolic planning framework that supports refining action plans and evolving the symbolic world, i.e., the symbolic representations of open-ended environments. SCOPE comprises two synergistic modules: a Symbolic Execution Simulator (SESim) that conducts symbolic validation and real execution of action plans, leveraging the feedback to refine the plans and evolve the symbolic world; and a Self-Adaptive Symbolic Memory (SASMem) that further distills feedback into evolving symbolic knowledge to enhance long-horizon planning and modeling of the symbolic world. Experiments in open-ended environments show that SCOPE significantly improves the completeness of the symbolic world, the success rate of plans under environment perturbations, and cross-task grounding and adaptability across diverse embodied scenarios.
